title: Homemade lemonade
intro: Peel steeped in the syrup brings aroma; fresh juice brings the sharpness.

steps.t: Wash the lemons and peel strips of zest from 2 with a peeler, avoiding the white pith.
Warm 200 ml water with the sugar and zest in a small pan, stirring until the sugar dissolves.
Turn off the heat and let the zest steep for 15 minutes.
steps.label: Infuse

steps.t: Meanwhile, juice all the lemons and strain: you need about 160 ml.
In a jug, combine the strained syrup, lemon juice and cold water; stir.
Chill in the fridge for at least 1 hour.
steps.label: Chill

steps.t: Serve over ice with a few mint leaves.

tips.t: Top with sparkling water just before serving for a fizzy lemonade.
It keeps for 3 days in a sealed bottle in the fridge.
A sprig of rosemary or thyme in the syrup gives it a garden scent.

title: Peach iced tea
intro: Made with real cooked peaches and briefly brewed black tea, never bitter.

steps.t: Chop the peaches with skin on, stone them and put them in a pan with the sugar and 200 ml water.
Cook over medium heat for 8 minutes, mashing with a fork, until the peaches fall apart.
steps.label: Peaches

steps.t: Meanwhile, heat 500 ml water to 95 °C, just short of boiling, turn off the heat and add the tea bags.
Steep for 4 minutes, then lift out the bags without squeezing them.
steps.label: Tea

steps.t: Strain the peaches, pressing hard with a spoon, and add the syrup to the tea.
Add 300 ml cold water and the lemon juice, then chill for 2 hours.
steps.label: Chill

steps.t: Serve over ice with a few slices of fresh peach.

tips.t: Don't squeeze the tea bags: the tannins make the tea bitter and cloudy.
Green tea brewed at 80 °C with white peaches makes a gentler version.

title: Watermelon agua fresca
intro: Watermelon blended with lime and water: summer in a Mexican market.

steps.t: Cube the watermelon and remove as many black seeds as you can.
Blend the watermelon, water, lime juice and sugar for 30 seconds.
Strain through a sieve to remove the pulp and pour into a jug.
Chill in the fridge for 30 minutes.
steps.label: Chill

steps.t: Stir, since it separates, and serve over ice with mint leaves.

tips.t: Same method works with melon, pineapple or cucumber: just swap the fruit.
Wet the glass rim with lime and dip it in salt and chilli powder.

title: Homemade ginger soda
intro: Fresh ginger syrup and sparkling water, with the bite of a ginger beer.

steps.t: Wash the ginger and grate it, skin and all.
Put the ginger, sugar and water in a pan, bring to a boil and simmer for 10 minutes.
steps.label: Syrup

steps.t: Turn off the heat and steep for 20 minutes; the longer it sits, the hotter it gets.
steps.label: Infuse

steps.t: Strain, pressing the ginger with a spoon, and chill the syrup for 30 minutes.
steps.label: Chill

steps.t: In each glass put ice, 50 ml syrup, the juice of half a lime and 200 ml sparkling water.
Stir gently just once and serve right away, while it's fizzy.

tips.t: The syrup keeps for 2 weeks in a sealed jar in the fridge.
Use this soda instead of ginger beer in a Moscow Mule.
A dried chilli or 2 cloves in the syrup give it more bite.

title: Ayran (salted yogurt drink)
intro: Yogurt, cold water and salt whisked until foamy: savoury and thirst-quenching.

steps.t: Put the yogurt and salt in a jug and whisk until smooth.
Add the cold water a little at a time, whisking all the while.
Whisk hard for 1 minute, or blend for 20 seconds, until a layer of foam forms.
Pour into chilled glasses and finish with a pinch of dried mint.

tips.t: Serve with kebabs, köfte or anything spicy: it cools the palate.
Use sparkling water instead of still and it's close to Persian doogh.
